references.text: Abraham also hurried to prepare food for his heavenly guests, including bread and meat, in a similar way as Gideon here prepares a meal for the Lord's angel.
Unleavened bread (mazzot) was prescribed during the Passover meal, and Gideon uses it when he prepares his offering.
Unleavened bread made from fine flour is also used in connection with the consecration offering for the priests.
An ephah of flour for unleavened bread is a standard amount used in the grain offering, just as Gideon here uses an ephah of flour.
Manoah, Samson's father, also prepares a young goat and unleavened bread for the Lord's angel in a very similar way to what Gideon does here.
Hannah also uses an ephah of flour when she brings Samuel to the temple, a corresponding amount to what Gideon uses.
Abraham received his guests under a tree, just as Gideon here meets the angel under the terebinth (oak).
